whatIs: readme.so is a browser-based editor for building a project's README: you pick sections from a list, such as Installation, Usage/Examples, API Reference or License, edit them and see the result in a preview or as raw Markdown.
It's a good fit when you want a complete, well-organized README without starting from a blank page, or when you need a GitHub profile with introduction sections.
uses: Building the README for a new project by adding installation, usage and license.
Creating your GitHub profile README with introduction, skills and links sections.
Standardizing the README across several repositories starting from the same sections.
caveats: The sections are generic: you have to replace the sample text with real information about your project.
Check the Raw view before downloading, because the final Markdown is what will be published in your repository.
It doesn't connect to GitHub: you download the file or copy the Markdown and upload it to the repository yourself.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license, with no paid plans.
idealFor: People who want a tidy README without writing it from scratch.
